strings.name: Michael Bloomberg
strings.role: Bloomberg co-founder · Former New York mayor and philanthropist
strings.summary: Michael Bloomberg combined financial data, analysis and news in Bloomberg’s business and served as New York City mayor from 2002 to 2013. He advanced public-health, city-management and climate initiatives, while expanded stop-and-frisk policing under his administration faced constitutional criticism in court. After office, he continued education and health philanthropy and sought the Democratic presidential nomination.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026, including the 2025–2026 philanthropy report. The timeline selects milestones through the 2024 gift. Civic achievements, disputes and court findings are distinguished; influence does not imply endorsement.
strings.influence.rationale: Co-founded Bloomberg, integrating financial data, news and analytics into global financial workflows.

strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Financial information services
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Co-built Bloomberg, integrating market data, analytics and news into financial workflows worldwide.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Public health and education
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Funded public health, climate action and student financial assistance through philanthropic programs.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Medical and graduate education gift
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Bloomberg Philanthropies gave Johns Hopkins $1 billion to expand aid for medical and other graduate students.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: Leaves presidential primary
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Ended his campaign for the Democratic presidential nomination.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Undergraduate financial aid
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Gave Johns Hopkins $1.8 billion to support need-blind admissions and financial assistance.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Mayoral term ends amid policing debate
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Completed three terms; a federal court found aspects of NYPD stop-and-frisk practices unconstitutional.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Becomes New York mayor
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Began the first of three terms, serving through the end of 2013.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Bloomberg News established
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Expanded financial reporting with his team, connecting terminal data with news.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Co-founds information business
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Started the business that became Bloomberg L.P. after leaving Salomon Brothers.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: MBA and start in finance
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Graduated from Harvard Business School and began his career at Salomon Brothers.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: Born in Boston
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Grew up in Massachusetts and later studied electrical engineering at Johns Hopkins.
